subject: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)

messages.author: 659ec85b628948d3
messages.subject: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)
parts:
Hi Meena and Olga,

I've started using MSStats (V.3.5.6) to analyse my DIA/SWATH data (25 healthy, 25 disease - 3 injection replicates).
I used a blocking during sample prep and runs - as I learned from Olga on last year's proteomics course.

Questions:
  1. Does MSStats automatically use fragments only when summing intensities or will precursors get included if present in MSStatsInput.csv? My Skyline MSStatsInput shows fragments and precursors (because I've chosen to show precursors in skyline) but I'm pretty sure that DIA analysis should be carried out using fragments only.
  2. With regard to my experiment, how do I best normalize? Is median normalization ok in label-free DIA data? I have some heavy SIS peptides spiked-in that I could potentially use.
  3. I would like to compare healthy and disease (2 conditions) and on top of that compare a specific influence of genotype (3 conditions - GG, GC, CC) within Healthy and Disease. Can I do this in MSStats.

Please let me know if you need further detail or files made available.

Regards

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)
parts:
Please see below: 

1. MSstats uses fragments for summarization. 

2. It should be okay, and you may want to cross check the normalization results with both options. It's usually a good idea to check the profile plots (before and after normalization) of some proteins that you know well. 

3. It's possible - you'll need to provide the genotype in the Condition column, and specify the comparisons you'd like to make by defining the contrast matrix (see 4.1.6 of the document at http://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/MSstats_v3.6_manual.pdf)

HTH
Tsung-Heng
